# Java Audiveris 5.11 (JDK 25) per-spot beam recognition for chula.png,
# sheet 1, from oracle/java/BeamsProbe.java.
#
# oracle/beams-chula.txt pins the SIG at the *end* of BEAMS, three stages
# downstream of recognition -- extension, hooks and grouping all add and remove
# beams after the fact. So a port whose per-spot recognition is perfect and
# whose extension is missing looks, in that oracle, like a port that cannot
# recognise beams at all. This one stops at createBeamInters and reports per
# spot, so the two can be told apart.
#
#   sheet <file>#<n> interline <i> beam <b> smallBeam <s>
#   itemparam  <name> <value>    -- BeamsBuilder.ItemParameters, as Java scales
#   sheetparam <name> <value>    -- BeamsBuilder.Parameters
#   spot <i> system <s> <x> <y> <w> <h> <weight>
#   reject <i> <reason>          -- one of checkBeamGlyph's six named refusals
#   meanheight <i> <v>           -- glyph mean thickness, the "too slim" test
#   meandist <i> <v>             -- computeLines, the "wavy borders" test
#   structwidth <i> <v>          -- the "too narrow width" test
#   slopegap <i> <v>             -- compareSlopes, the "diverging beams" test
#   line <spot> <l> <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2> <height>
#   item <spot> <l> <i> <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2> <height>
#   jitter <spot> <top> <bottom> <distImpact>
#   rawbeam <system> <class> <shape> <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2> <height>
#           grade <g> impacts wdth <v> minH <v> maxH <v> core <v> belt <v> jit <v>
#
# `rawbeam` is what createBeamInters produced, before extendBeams, buildHooks
# or grouping touched anything, obtained by replaying buildBeams' own prefix and
# calling createBeams reflectively. On this page it is 91 BeamInter and 20
# BeamHookInter -- and oracle/beams-chula.txt ends the step with 91 beams and 31
# hooks, so *every* beam comes from here and extension adds none. Only the hooks
# grow. That is worth knowing before porting extendBeams: it is not on the path
# to the beams themselves on this page.
#   premedian <spot> <l> <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2>   -- before adjustSides
#   section <spot> <l> <i> <x> <y> <w> <h> <centreX> <yOnMedian> <contains>
#
# The last two are printed with Double.toString rather than %.9f, and that is
# the point. retrieveItems decides where a beam item starts by asking whether a
# section's centre lies on the median, against the median computeLines produced
# and *not* the adjusted one, and the test is half-open. On this page one such
# query gives y = 924.9999999999998 against a run ending at 924: inside by one
# ulp. Printed to nine decimals it reads 925.000000000, which is outside, and a
# port that matched the printed value would start that beam a section late.
#
# The rejections are half the value here. Java refuses a spot for a named
# reason before any structure exists, and a port that accepts a spot Java
# refused is wrong in a way no accepted-beam comparison would ever show. On
# this page 211 of 318 dispatched spots are refused, and every intermediate the
# refusals test is pinned beside them.
#
# Spot indices run across systems in Java's own per-system order, which is
# Glyphs.byFullOrdinate rather than by abscissa. A spot straddling two systems
# is dispatched to both and appears twice, which is why there are 318 here and
# 305 in oracle/beam-spots.txt.
#
# The probe reaches STEM_SEEDS and then runs BeamsStep's prolog itself, rather
# than reaching BEAMS: the step's own epilog removes every BEAM_SPOT glyph, so
sheet chula.png#1 interline 21 beam 12 smallBeam null
